newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Command leaps after Cairn merger bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Command leaps after Cairn merger bid.

text.p: Shares in oil producer Command Petroleum Ltd leapt 19 cents or 19.6 percent to A$1.16 in early Thursday trade after it announced late on Wednesday it had agreed to merge with British oil producer Cairn Energy Plc.
Command said the A$1.10 per share cash offer from Cairn valued it at A$365 million, while the two Cairn shares for every 13 Command shares scrip offer valued the group at A$375 million.
Analysts said the premium being paid for Command was due to speculation among some traders and investors that another company might offer a higher price, scuttling the friendly takeover.
"What these punters are doing is basing on the fact that there may be a higher bid to come through and that this is just the opening gambit," one analyst said.
John Hirgee, an analyst for First Pacific Stockbroking, said it was too early too tell whether Command shareholders will opt for cash or Cairn scrip.
"They may want to take the money and run or participate in what Cairn's wants to do to further their projects," he said.
However, "Australian fund managers are likely to take the money rather than get into something in the U.K. that is not covered here".
Still, Hirgee said the deal made sense, given Cairn's ability to inject capital into Command.

SOCO Australia Pty Ltd, a unit of Snyder Oil Corp, will allow Cairn's to acquire 19.9 percent of Command in return for an issue of shares on terms equivalent to the share offer. Snyder has a total stake of 32.6 percent.
Snyder has advised that in the absence of a better offer, it intends to accept the Cairn offer for the balance of its holding and expects to take Cairn shares.
Command is the operator of the Ravva oilfield off the coast of India while Cairn is developing the Sangu field off the Bangladesh coast and also has North Sea production assets.
